title: Zeros to the End
statement:
Return a list with the same numbers as `numbers`, but with every `0` moved to the **end**, while all the other numbers keep their original relative order.

Try to do it in a single pass without building a second list of the non-zero numbers.

examples.explanation: 5 and 7 keep their order; the three zeros go to the end.
There are no zeros: nothing moves.

hints.nudge: Keep a position `write` where the next non-zero number belongs. What do you do when you meet a non-zero number?
hints.pattern: Two pointers: `read` scans the list; `write` marks the first zero (or the next free spot). Swap non-zero numbers forward into the write position.
hints.walkthrough: Everything before `write` is already final: non-zero numbers in their original order. When `read` finds a non-zero number, swap it with whatever is at `write` (a zero, or itself when no zero has been passed yet) and move `write` forward. Zeros are never moved explicitly; they simply get pushed back by the swaps, and each stays after all the non-zeros that came before it. The relative order of the non-zero numbers is kept because they are placed in the order they are read. One pass, O(n) time, O(1) extra space. Counting the non-zeros and filling the rest with zeros also works if you may write over the list.
